name: menu
description: UIDS menu component contract, preserving the verified 4.x rendering and documenting the proposed Figma representation.

figma.note: BUILT (Phase 3). 6 variants, SPARSE: Orientation x Nesting x State = 8 naive, minus the 2 Horizontal+Nested cells. So Horizontal x Top-level x {Default, Active} (2) and Vertical x {Top-level, Nested} x {Default, Active} (4).
axisRationale: Hover is NOT an axis value, following Button — whose set is Color x Size x Style with no interaction-state axis at all; hover and focus are documented in prose. Menu's hover is also selector-scoped to top-level links only (`> li > a:hover:after`, menu.scss:119), so a Nested+Hover cell would have to render identically to Default. An annotated example frame shows the top-level gold-indicator treatment instead (the Headline 'context frames, not axes' precedent).

Horizontal x Nested is EXCLUDED: `.menu--horizontal`'s `> li ul { display: none; }` (menu.scss:145-147) means nested items never render in horizontal mode, so the cell would depict something the live component can never show.
Icon presence and children/chevron presence stay boolean instance-swap SLOT properties, not variant axes (Button's icon-slot precedent) — both are content-driven per `items`, not a style choice.
figma.precedent: Button (no interaction-state axis); Form Item (sparse set); Headline (context frames, not axes).

options.name: items
options.description: Keys per item, spread straight onto a nested MenuItem via v-bind (Menu.vue:54,62): label (required), url, children (a nested array of the same shape, which is what produces the submenu tree), active, expanded, icon. NOTE `variant` is a MenuItem prop but is supplied by Menu itself, not by the item. Required, with no default: the component renders nothing without it. Added 2026-08-20 to close the long-standing check-contracts warning that this Vue prop was unclaimed by any contract option — the schema already supported array/object option types.

code.notes: Vue marks it required:true with type:Array and no default.

figma.notes: Content, not a variant axis: the number of entries drives how many rows/tabs/crumbs are drawn, which Figma expresses by duplicating the child instance rather than by a variant property.

options.name: variant
options.description: Menu's own orientation switch (Menu.vue only — MenuItem.vue has NO variant prop at all, see claims). Only 'horizontal' pushes an extra class (`menu--${className(variant)}` = menu--horizontal, Menu.vue:37-45); 'vertical' emits no modifier class — the base .menu rule already IS vertical, the same intentionally-undefined-modifier pattern as Button's size=medium.

code.notes: MenuItem.vue's recursive nested <Menu> ALWAYS hardcodes variant="vertical" (MenuItem.vue:67) regardless of the parent menu's own variant. MenuItem.vue's OWN liClasses computed also checks `props.variant === 'horizontal'` (MenuItem.vue:39) but MenuItem declares no such prop — see claims (dead-code).

options.name: top
options.description: Whether to wrap the rendered <ul> in a `<nav :aria-label="label">` landmark (Menu.vue:49) instead of a bare <ul> (Menu.vue:58). Defaults to FALSE. Every recursive nested <Menu> that MenuItem.vue renders (MenuItem.vue:65-68) omits `top` entirely, so by construction only an explicit root-level call can ever produce a landmark.

figma.notes: Structural wrapper presence, not a visual style — represent as a landmark annotation on the outer frame, not a variant axis.

options.name: label
options.description: ROOT-LEVEL aria-label text for the <nav>, read only when top=true (Menu.vue:31-34,49). Defaults to '' — see knownIssues for the resulting aria-label="" gap. DISTINCT from each entry in `items`, which also has its own `label` field (the rendered link text, on MenuItem.vue) — same prop name, two entirely different roles.

figma.notes: Non-visual landmark label; not represented as a bindable text layer.

behavior: Menu.vue and MenuItem.vue render ZERO real Vue <slot> elements — unlike every other migrated component (Button/Headline both wrap a default slot), all content is data-driven through the `items` prop. This is the first component in the family with no slot at all.

Top-level-only bold: `:not(ul ul):not(.menu--horizontal) > li > a` (menu.scss:19-21) applies font-weight 500 ONLY to vertical, non-nested links. Nested links and horizontal-mode links have no explicit weight anywhere in this file and inherit the ambient default.

Indicator mechanics (`&:after` on every link, menu.scss:76-88): 0-size + `--uids-gray-light` background at ALL depths by default. `.is-active` (menu.scss:51-59, ANY depth) forces full-size via the transform-end variable but does NOT touch color, so a NESTED active item shows a GRAY indicator, not gold. GOLD hover fires via `> li > a:hover:after` (menu.scss:119-124). CORRECTED 2026-08-17: that combinator does NOT confine gold to top-level links. `Menu.vue` unconditionally pushes `'menu'` (Menu.vue:38) and `MenuItem.vue` recurses into `<Menu variant="vertical">` (MenuItem.vue:64-67), so EVERY nested submenu is a `<ul class="menu">` — a nested link is a direct child of its OWN `.menu`, hovering gold at any depth. Verified live: a nested link (`Undergraduate`) returns true for `element.matches('.menu > li > a')`. Do not read `>` as anchoring to the outermost menu. Second-order: behavior[9].

`.menu--horizontal` (menu.scss:127-149) is entirely gated behind `utilities.container-query()` at its default parameter (`variables.$break-sm` = 768px; menu.scss:128, _breakpoints.scss:52) — progressively enhanced from `@container column (min-width:768px)` when an ancestor establishes that container context, down to a plain `@media (min-width:768px)` fallback under `@supports not (contain: inline-size)`. Menu.stories.js's own wrapper, `<div class="column-container">` (Menu.stories.js:29), DOES establish this context (`.column-container { container-type: inline-size; container-name: column; }`, _grid.scss:78-84) — so capturing the standard 375/980/1350 regression viewports against that story is a valid proxy for the container's actual inline-size here. Below 768px (container), `.menu--horizontal` renders IDENTICAL to a vertical menu.

`.menu--horizontal` unconditionally hides ALL nested submenus (`> li ul { display: none; }`, menu.scss:145-147), with a documented @todo about WCAG 2.1 hover/focus content (menu.scss:143-144). MenuItem's recursive <Menu variant="vertical"> still renders in the DOM at any nesting depth — it is CSS-hidden, not markup-absent — so a horizontal-mode Figma variant with nested children should show them as absent/hidden, not omit the underlying structure.

MenuItem renders either <a :href="url"> or, when `url` is falsy, a plain non-interactive <span> with otherwise identical content (MenuItem.vue:53-62) — a 'headless group-label' pattern for items that exist only to hold `children`. Zero current fixture data (Menu.stories.js, both Showcase stories) exercises an item with `children` but no `url` — see storyAudit.

`top` defaults to false and every recursive nested <Menu> call omits it entirely (MenuItem.vue:65-68) — by construction, only the single outermost call can ever produce the <nav> landmark. Menu.stories.js's Template hardcodes :top="true" (Menu.stories.js:30) for both exports, masking this default in the only dedicated stories that exist.
When top=true and label is left at its default '', the rendered markup is <nav aria-label=""> (Menu.vue:31-34,49) rather than an unlabeled <nav> — see knownIssues.

`.fa-li`'s `position: absolute` comes from Font Awesome 5's own CSS (an external runtime dependency) — UIDS's menu.scss only overrides its `left` offset (menu.scss:42-44). No `.fa-ul` ancestor class is ever applied by Menu.vue/MenuItem.vue (confirmed: zero occurrences in src/), but Menu's own `li { position: relative; }` (menu.scss:28, applies to EVERY li unconditionally) already supplies the positioning context Font Awesome's `.fa-ul > li` rule would otherwise provide, so the icon still positions correctly without it.

SECOND-ORDER CONSEQUENCE of behavior[2]: `.menu li.is-active a:after` and `.menu > li > a:hover:after` have equal specificity (0,2,3), so source order decides and the hover rule (declared later) wins — hovering the CURRENT item turns its gray indicator gold.
knownIssues: MenuItem.vue's `expanded` prop (default false, MenuItem.vue:18-21) sets `.is-expanded` (MenuItem.vue:45) which matches no CSS selector anywhere in the repo — plumbed but visually inert. It also cannot function as an accordion-style collapse toggle even at the markup level: the recursive <Menu v-if="children && children.length"> (MenuItem.vue:65) renders unconditionally whenever children exist, never gated on `expanded`. See claims.

`.user-menu-toggle { .menu { display: none; } }` (menu.scss:151-154) has no companion rule that ever reveals the menu again, and no JS behavior class (accordion.js/tabs.js/slider.js/video.js/click-a11y.js — none reference "menu"/"nav"/"toggle" relevantly) wires one up. The pattern shown in ApplicationForm.stories.js:63-76 (a 'HawkID' account button beside a hidden <ul class="menu"> sign-out link) can only ever render in its closed state as currently shipped. See claims.

`top` defaults to false (a caller who omits it gets a bare <ul>, no <nav> landmark at all) and, separately, a caller who passes top=true without label gets aria-label="" rather than no attribute (Menu.vue:27-34,49) — the empty string is arguably a worse outcome for assistive technology than omitting the attribute entirely. Both defaults are masked by Menu.stories.js hardcoding :top="true" in its Template (Menu.stories.js:30).
`.icon-after` (MenuItem.vue:56 and :61, on the chevron <span>) matches no CSS rule anywhere in src/scss/ — an unstyled hook.

`const name = 'uids-menu'` (Menu.vue:7) is declared and never read anywhere else in the file — same dead-code shape as the already-documented unused `const name` in Button.vue, PseudoButton.vue, and Headline.vue.

brand-footer.scss (`.footer__links .menu` at brand-footer.scss:111-132) overrides `.menu a`'s font-weight/color/font-size directly on nested selectors, bypassing Menu's own --menu-* custom properties entirely — and brand-footer's OWN contract (contracts/brand-footer.json) already claims the tier-3 tokens brand-footer/menu/font-size, brand-footer/menu/font-weight, brand-footer/menu/link-color for exactly this override (tokens/components/brand-footer.json's 'menu' block). Menu's new contract must NOT re-claim those names — check-contracts.mjs enforces one-contract-per-token. brand-footer.scss itself should NOT be added to Menu's identity.relatedPaths (it's brand-footer's own claimed territory) — this is a plain cross-reference, matching the pattern already used for Brand Bar/Logo.

docroot/themes/custom/uids_base/templates/navigation/menu.html.twig and menu--top-links.html.twig (verified in /Users/bspeare/acquia/uiowa) render real Drupal menus with a plain class="menu" — genuine downstream consumption of this contract's base class, independent of the Vue component. Proposed as identity.downstreamPaths when the real contract is authored — see openQuestions (not identified by the input survey; flagging as a recommendation, not a confirmed requirement). Separately, uids_base/uids/ (this repo's own components/scss vendored into uids_base) is a byte-identical mirror of menu.scss/Menu.vue/MenuItem.vue/Menu.stories.js (diff exit 0) — not a second implementation, not drift.

There is no token for the ACTIVE link-indicator colour. menu/link-indicator/hover-color exists (gold), but `.is-active a:after` inherits the base `background: var(--uids-gray-light)` (#CACACA) -- verified live: active computes rgb(202,202,202), gold is hover-only. The Figma component binds the indicator to the color/gray/200 primitive (legal: check-figma's tokensUsed rule only constrains component-tier bindings). Ruled 2026-08-16: record rather than add a token now.

The mobile 'MENU' accordion on live sites — the full-width bar that collapses the primary nav below the sm breakpoint and toggles it open — is DOWNSTREAM-ONLY and cannot be rebuilt from UIDS as shipped. uids_base owns both halves: templates/navigation/toggle-nav--bttn.twig renders the toggle (a button.toggle-nav__bttn holding `Menu`) and assets/js/toggle-nav.js, attached via uids_base.libraries.yml, drives the open/close — all three verified in /Users/bspeare/acquia/uiowa. UIDS has no reveal even at the markup level: knownIssues[0] records that `expanded` gates nothing, and knownIssues[1] that the one hide rule has no companion reveal and no behavior JS references the menu. Recorded 2026-09-02 so nobody rebuilds it here — it is uids_base territory, the same boundary as the layout--title classes (detected downstream, not authored).
changes: 2026-09-02 — RETIRED the knownIssues entry claiming `.menu--container` had no dedicated story and no regression coverage. False on every count when checked: Menu.stories.js exports `Container` (a dedicated .menu--container story), regression/config.json samples `.menu--container` border width/style/colour against it, and regression/baselines/menu.json holds the border OBSERVED at rgb(230,229,229) at 375/980/1350 — the observation that settled the nav-strip border token (rules.json nav-strip-border-is-full-bleed). The entry also still pointed at 'a proposed new story' that had since been written. What remains true — the class is consumed by the two Application showcase stories — is derivable by grep and needs no knownIssue. Deleted rather than amended because every load-bearing clause was false; this entry is the paper trail.

geometryNotTokenized.orientation-axis-switch: --menu-flex-direction (column/row, menu.scss:5,131) plus the indicator's scaleX/scaleY transform-start/end custom properties (menu.scss:9-10,132-133) are structural axis-switch mechanics, not design values — same treatment as Brand Bar's tab-overhang geometry. Only the indicator's THICKNESS (menu/link-indicator/thickness) and its two colors are tokenized; which CSS property (width vs. height) carries that thickness, and which transform axis animates it, per orientation, stays raw.
geometryNotTokenized.shared-core-custom-properties: --uids-gray-cool (.fas icon color, menu.scss:47) and --uids-gray-light (indicator default background, menu.scss:77) are NOT menu tokens. Both are legacy custom-property names in uids-core.scss that already alias the generated primitives — verified: uids-core.scss:24 `--uids-gray-cool: var(--uiowa-color-gray-500);`, uids-core.scss:31 `--uids-gray-light: var(--uiowa-color-gray-200);`. Same treatment as Button's --transparent-border.
geometryNotTokenized.has-icon-indent: padding-left: 3.1rem (`.has-icon > a`, `> span:not([class*="fa"])`, rule at menu.scss:35-40, property at :38) — one-off icon-indent offset. Sits close to but does NOT equal $xxlg (3.15rem, itself already flagged zero-use/deletion-candidate in tokens/README) — kept raw rather than promoted; see openQuestions.
geometryNotTokenized.icon-position: `.fa-li { left: .9rem; }` (menu.scss:42-44) positions the icon glyph; position:absolute itself comes from Font Awesome 5's own CSS, an external runtime dependency (see behavior). The .9rem value exactly matches $sm-md — tracked in sharedPrimitiveUsage, not tokenized here as its own leaf.
geometryNotTokenized.nested-indent: margin-left: 1.7rem on `& > ul.menu` (menu.scss:100-102) — nested-menu indentation. No primitive matches (nearest is $xlg at 2.5rem).
geometryNotTokenized.border-widths: Both borders in this file are 1px (li separator menu.scss:24, .menu--container menu.scss:158) — only their COLOR is tokenized, matching Button's `border: 1px solid var(--transparent-border)` precedent.
geometryNotTokenized.hover-transition: transition: 0.3s all ease-in-out (+ -webkit- prefix) on the indicator &:after (menu.scss:86-87) — animation timing, not a design value, same treatment as Button's focus-bar-motion.
geometryNotTokenized.horizontal-mode-layout: display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; (menu.scss:134-135) and the removal of li border-bottom (menu.scss:138-140) inside .menu--horizontal are structural layout mechanics, not component-identity values.
